newsitem.title: CANADA: TCPL shippers want 2 BCF of '98 transport.
newsitem.headline: TCPL shippers want 2 BCF of '98 transport.

text.p: TransCanada PipeLines Ltd said its just-completed open season attracted requests from shippers for well over two billion cubic feet per day of new natural gas transport capacity starting in November 1998.
TransCanada, which operates Canada's main west-east gas pipeline system, said shippers would be completing the paperwork for their service requests over the next month.
The documentation would form the basis for the company's 1998 facilities application to Canada's National Energy Board, it said.
"We believe this is a strong, market-driven response to the need for additional pipeline capacity out of Alberta," TransCanada chief executive George Watson said in a statement.
A scarcity of take-away pipeline space has often been blamed for western Canadian natural gas prices that are well below those in eastern North America.

TransCanada is currently seeking NEB approval to build C$899 million worth of new pipeline and compression facilities in 1997. The project, if approved, would add new firm transport service totalling 286.7 million cubic feet per day by November of that year.
TransCanada said that its system last year moved more than 2.35 trillion cubic feet of gas, which was over 10 percent of total North American demand.

For its open season, TransCanada garnered over 100 requests for service for the contract year starting November 1998 from 60 companies, it said. Eighty percent of the requests were for exports to the United States and the remainder for the Canadian market.
The company said its shippers could also submit requests for service through this month for contract years starting November 1999. -- Reuters Calgary Bureau 403 531-1624
